reader.requirement: At --std 85 an FD for a relative or indexed file must admit exactly the Format 2 clauses (IS EXTERNAL, IS GLOBAL, BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD in all forms, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS) and refuse LINAGE, CODE-SET and REPORT, which Format 2 does not print.

CODE-SET national phrases (alphabet-name-2 / FOR) refused below 2002; the single-name '85 form is admitted at every edition
DialectBehavior.RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize (RECORD CONTAINS m TO n bounds a WRITE only from 2002); not part of format admission

reader.notes: FileDescriptionFormats.Of makes any relative or indexed file Format 2 whatever else the FD says, so LINAGE, CODE-SET and REPORT are refused by the one table (COBOL2604) and not bound. The diagnostic quotes the 2023 clause list (it omits LABEL/VALUE OF/DATA RECORDS by design), which is only wording at 85.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:X.4.2.2 Format 2 (no LINAGE, CODE-SET, REPORT). Probes at --std 85: g2ord.cob (indexed FD with DATA RECORD first, RECORD IS VARYING FROM 4 TO 10 DEPENDING ON WLEN, VALUE OF FILE-ID IS data-name, IS GLOBAL, LABEL, BLOCK 2 TO 4 RECORDS; relative FD LABEL/RECORD/BLOCK in a different order) compiled and ran '[K001DAT   ] 07 / DONE' (7-character varying record written and read back, WLEN set to 7); g2bad.cob refused CODE-SET on INDEXED (COBOL2604, the reader probed it only on RELATIVE), LINAGE on RELATIVE (COBOL2604, the reader probed it only on INDEXED), and FORMAT CHARACTER DATA on INDEXED (COBOL2604 plus COBOL0900). The repeat screen (COBOL2423) and integer-operand screen shown under SR1 run on the same FD clause loop for every organization. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.4.2.3 SR2  (4.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'.
